title: E-Math mensuration: sectors, pyramids and spheres
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can apply the angle-over-360 fraction to both arc length and sector area.
The class can state the pyramid and sphere volume formulae and substitute the radius or base area correctly.

modelAnswers.question: Find the volume of a square pyramid whose base is 6 cm by 6 cm and whose vertical height is 4 cm.
Find the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm, in terms of pi.

commonErrors.misconception: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that circle B, radius 6 cm, has double the area of circle A, radius 3 cm.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: work out both areas using r squared first, 9 pi against 36 pi, then state the multiplier.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: area scales with r squared, so doubling the radius quadruples the area, from 9 pi to 36 pi.

commonErrors.misconception: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner agrees that enlarging a circle from radius 5 cm to 10 cm doubles its area.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: work out both areas, 25 pi and 100 pi, and check their ratio before answering.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: 100 pi is four times 25 pi, so the area has quadrupled, not doubled.

nextSteps: Reteach the trap, landing that area scales with the square of the radius: double the radius and the area quadruples.
Practise the sector fraction from the worked example - write angle over 360 first, then apply it to the circumference or the circle area.
